title: Make the settlement gate tell the on-call who is inside

blocks.text: The nightly settlement jobs all append to one ledger file, so each job runs through a `Gate` that lets one job in at a time. Last night settlement hung. The ops dashboard, which reads `ThreadMXBean`, showed six job threads `RUNNABLE` at full CPU inside `Gate.inside` and no thread owning anything; it took an hour of reading stacks to find `settle-eu`, the job that was inside, waiting on a file share. The same week, a job that threw on a malformed ledger line was followed by a gate nobody could get through.

Rewrite `inside` in `src/main/java/practice/Gate.java`. When you're done, jobs still run one at a time; a thread waiting at the gate is reported by `ThreadMXBean` as waiting for a lock, held by the thread of the job that is inside; and a job that throws passes its exception to its caller without keeping the gate closed for the next job. About three lines.

cases.says: inside(job) runs the job and returns its result
twenty thousand jobs from four threads run one at a time, so none of their updates is lost
a thread waiting at the gate is reported by ThreadMXBean as waiting for a lock held by the job's thread inside
a job that throws passes its exception to its caller, and the next job, on another thread, still gets in

origin.section: A Thread Dump Names a Monitor's Holder; a Hand-Rolled Lock Shows Only Busy Threads

concepts: A thread waiting on a monitor or a java.util.concurrent lock is reported with the holder's name; a thread spinning on a hand-rolled atomic lock shows as RUNNABLE with no owner.
A synchronized method or block releases its monitor when the body throws; a hand-written lock is released only by a finally the caller wrote.
